summary: Economics professor Antonio Salazar ruled Portugal as dictator from 1932 to 1968, running the Estado Novo with a torturing secret police and waging ruinous colonial wars in Angola and Mozambique.

evidence.note: Salazar born in 1889 in the village of Vimieiro
Carmona becomes president in 1928 and hands Salazar control of the finances
Estado Novo proclaimed in 1933 with Salazar holding full power
New constitution creates the PVDE secret police; torture at Aljube and the statue method
Aid to Franco in the Spanish Civil War, then keeping Spain neutral in WWII with British help
CIA trains the secret police in interrogation from 1957, including sound-based torture
Regime adopts lusotropicalism to justify keeping the empire
Segment on Portugal's slave trading and later forced labour laws in Angola and Mozambique
1961 uprisings in Angola open the colonial war
1968 cerebral haemorrhage ends his rule; death in 1970 follows

notes: main_span ends 1968, when the stroke removed him from power; death in 1970 is in covered_span. The 1974 Carnation Revolution gets only a short coda. A short passage on systematic rape by Portuguese soldiers in Angola may justify sexual-violence; left out as brief. Goa (IN) and US CIA training are short and not in setting.
